blocks.zh: 本節學習目標
blocks.en: Learning Objectives for This Section

blocks.zh: 理解 ICH 成員區域（美國、歐盟、日本、加拿大、瑞士）的 PAC 申報分類差異，以及 CDMO 同步管理多地區申報的核心挑戰。
blocks.en: Understand how post-approval change (PAC) filing categories differ across the ICH member regions (US, EU, Japan, Canada, Switzerland), and the core challenge for a CDMO of managing filings in several regions in parallel.

blocks.zh: 掌握非 ICH 地區（巴西、中國、印度、台灣等）在 PAC 審查時程與資料要求上的特殊性，及其對供應鏈的潛在衝擊。
blocks.en: Understand the particular features of PAC review timelines and data requirements in non-ICH regions (Brazil, China, India, Taiwan, etc.), and their potential impact on the supply chain.

blocks.zh: 了解既有上市產品（Legacy Products）導入 ICH Q12 EC 架構時的實務困難與補充申報策略。
blocks.en: Understand the practical difficulties of introducing the ICH Q12 EC framework for legacy marketed products, and the supplemental filing strategy.

blocks.zh: 熟悉 PDA 對全球法規調和的具體建議，包括統一變更定義、審查時程標準化，以及相互認可機制的潛力。
blocks.en: Know PDA's specific recommendations for global regulatory harmonization, including harmonized change definitions, standardized review timelines, and the potential of mutual recognition mechanisms.

blocks.zh: 掌握 CDMO 共用設施／設備的 PAC 管理複雜度，以及 Site Master File（SMF）策略在多客戶環境下的關鍵角色。
blocks.en: Understand the complexity of PAC management for shared CDMO facilities and equipment, and the key role of a Site Master File (SMF) strategy in a multi-client environment.

blocks.zh: 6.0 Global Lifecycle and PAC Management 6.0 全球生命週期與核准後變更（PAC）管理
blocks.en: 6.0 Global Lifecycle and PAC Management

blocks.zh: 6.1 ICH Regions 6.1 ICH 區域
blocks.en: 6.1 ICH Regions

blocks.zh: 中文解說
blocks.en: Commentary

blocks.zh: 核心概念：ICH 成員區域的共同優勢
blocks.en: Core Concept: What ICH Member Regions Have in Common

blocks.zh: ICH（國際人用藥品技術要求協調委員會）成員目前涵蓋美國（FDA）、歐盟（EMA）、日本（PMDA）、加拿大（Health Canada）及瑞士（Swissmedic）等主要市場。
blocks.en: The ICH (International Council for Harmonisation of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use) members currently cover the major markets: the US (FDA), the EU (EMA), Japan (PMDA), Canada (Health Canada) and Switzerland (Swissmedic).

blocks.zh: 這些地區共享的關鍵特徵是：以風險為基礎的申報分類——同一類變更，可預期的審查路徑是相近的。例如某無菌生產設備的小幅改善，在美國可能走 CBE-30，在歐盟走 Type IB，在加拿大走 Level II，雖名稱不同，但背後邏輯一致。
blocks.en: The key shared feature of these regions is a risk-based filing categorization: the same type of change follows a broadly similar, predictable review path. For example, a minor improvement to sterile manufacturing equipment might be a CBE-30 in the US, a Type IB variation in the EU and a Level II change in Canada. The names differ, but the underlying logic is the same.

blocks.zh: 比喻：國際駕照 vs. 各國考照
blocks.en: Analogy: International Driving Permit vs. Taking the Test in Every Country

blocks.zh: ICH 成員就像承認國際駕照的國家——你在一個地方考過了，其他地方認可你的資格、審查你的資料時也用同樣的標準。非 ICH 地區則要求你重新從頭考試，且規則各地不同。
blocks.en: ICH members are like countries that recognize an international driving permit: once you have passed in one place, the others accept your qualification and apply the same standards when they assess your data. Non-ICH regions make you sit the test again from scratch, and the rules differ from place to place.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：CDMO 的多地區申報挑戰
blocks.en: Key Point: The CDMO's Multi-Region Filing Challenge

blocks.zh: 即使在 ICH 成員區域之間，同一個變更的申報類別仍可能不同：美國是 PAS（Prior Approval Supplement）、歐盟是 Type II、加拿大是 SNDS（Supplement to New Drug Submission）。CDMO 必須同步管理這些並行申報，時程、資料要求、審查回應各有差異。
blocks.en: Even among ICH member regions, the filing category for the same change can differ: in the US it is a PAS (Prior Approval Supplement), in the EU a Type II variation, and in Canada an SNDS (Supplement to New Drug Submission). A CDMO has to manage these parallel filings at the same time, each with its own timeline, data requirements and review responses.

blocks.zh: 思考練習
blocks.en: Reflection Exercise

blocks.zh: 你的廠區正要進行無菌充填設備的製程參數優化。這個變更需要同時向 FDA、EMA、Health Canada 申報。請思考：你會如何建立一套「一份科學論據，多地區申報包」的策略？哪些文件可以共用，哪些必須客製化？
blocks.en: Your site is about to optimize process parameters on a sterile filling line. The change must be filed with the FDA, EMA and Health Canada. Think about how you would build a "one scientific rationale, multiple regional filing packages" strategy. Which documents can be shared, and which must be tailored to each region?

blocks.zh: 6.2 Non-ICH Regions 6.2 非 ICH 區域
blocks.en: 6.2 Non-ICH Regions

blocks.zh: 核心概念：非 ICH 地區的四大挑戰
blocks.en: Core Concept: Four Major Challenges in Non-ICH Regions

blocks.zh: 缺乏申報指引：企業無法預測審查標準，容易被要求補充大量文件。
blocks.en: No filing guidance: companies cannot predict the review standards and are easily asked for large amounts of additional documents.

blocks.zh: 無低風險快速通道：即使是微小變更，也可能需要全面申請，無「告知即可」的通道。
blocks.en: No fast track for low-risk changes: even a minor change may require a full application, with no "notify only" route.

blocks.zh: 穩定性資料要求過高：小變更也可能要求完整效期（如 24 或 36 個月）的穩定性數據。
blocks.en: Excessive stability data requirements: even small changes may require stability data covering the full shelf life (e.g., 24 or 36 months).

blocks.zh: 大量輔助文件：公証文件、各類證書、合法化手續，每份都耗費時間與資源。
blocks.en: Large volumes of supporting documents: notarized documents, various certificates and legalization procedures each consume time and resources.

blocks.zh: 比喻：裝潢公司遇到不同建管局
blocks.en: Analogy: A Renovation Company Facing Different Building Authorities

blocks.zh: 想像你是一家裝潢公司，在台北改了一套標準施工流程。在台北（ICH 地區），只要備查就好；但在某些城市，你要重新送件、等 1-2 年、補送各種文件，還不能同時申請兩個工程的許可——每個案子只能一件一件慢慢排隊。
blocks.en: Imagine you run a renovation company and have changed a standard work procedure in Taipei. In Taipei (an ICH region), a simple notification is enough. In some other cities you have to resubmit everything, wait 1-2 years, supply a variety of extra documents, and you cannot even apply for permits for two projects at the same time: each case has to queue up one at a time.

blocks.zh: 這就是非 ICH 地區的 PAC 現實。
blocks.en: This is the reality of PAC in non-ICH regions.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：供應鏈的最高風險場景
blocks.en: Key Point: The Highest-Risk Supply Chain Scenario

blocks.zh: 最危險的情況是：製程已切換（舊流程不再使用）+ 審查延遲（長達數年）+ 產品效期短。舊庫存可能在新申請獲批之前就過期或耗盡，直接衝擊病患可及性。這正是 TR91 強調「提早聯繫非 ICH 法規機構」的原因。
blocks.en: The most dangerous situation is the combination of the process has already been switched (the old process is no longer used) + a delayed review (up to several years) + a short product shelf life. Old inventory may expire or run out before the new application is approved, directly affecting patient access. This is why TR91 stresses "contact non-ICH regulators early".

blocks.zh: WHO 指引的橋接價值
blocks.en: The Bridging Value of WHO Guidance

blocks.zh: 對於沒有自己 PAC 指引的國家，WHO 的生物製劑與疫苗 PAC 指引（TRS 993 & 1011）提供了一個風險分類框架。企業在申報時可主動引用這些指引，說明自身風險評估的依據，有助於縮短審查時間或建立溝通基礎。
blocks.en: For countries that have no PAC guidance of their own, the WHO guidelines on PACs for biotherapeutic products and vaccines (TRS 993 & 1011) provide a risk categorization framework. Companies can cite these guidelines proactively in their filings to explain the basis of their own risk assessment, which can help shorten review time or establish a basis for dialogue.

blocks.zh: CDMO 實務思考
blocks.en: CDMO Practical Reflection

blocks.zh: 你的客戶在台灣（非 ICH）、巴西（ANVISA）、印度（CDSCO）均有上市許可。一項共用設備的製程改善完成後，ICH 地區已獲批，但這三個市場仍在審查中。你如何管理這段「雙軌並存」的過渡期？哪些風險需要提前與客戶溝通？
blocks.en: Your client holds marketing authorizations in Taiwan (non-ICH), Brazil (ANVISA) and India (CDSCO). After a process improvement on shared equipment is completed, the ICH regions have approved it, but these three markets are still under review. How do you manage this "dual-track" transition period? Which risks should be raised with the client early?

blocks.zh: 7.0 Legacy Marketed Products and ICH Q12 7.0 既有上市產品與 ICH Q12
blocks.en: 7.0 Legacy Marketed Products and ICH Q12

blocks.zh: 核心概念：Legacy Products 的 ICH Q12 困境
blocks.en: Core Concept: The ICH Q12 Dilemma for Legacy Products

blocks.zh: ICH Q12 的精髓是「預先定義 Established Conditions（ECs）——哪些參數在 filing 裡、哪些只需 PQS 管理」。但這個框架對已上市的舊產品（Legacy Products）不是免費的：
blocks.en: The essence of ICH Q12 is to define Established Conditions (ECs) up front: which parameters are in the filing and which only need to be managed under the PQS. But this framework does not come free for older marketed products (legacy products):

blocks.zh: 舊 filing 沒有正式定義 ECs，必須回溯重建。
blocks.en: The old filing has no formally defined ECs, so they must be reconstructed retrospectively.

blocks.zh: 回溯需要大量歷史製造與特性化數據，並在 CTD Module 3.2.S.2.6 / 3.2.P.2 補充提交。
blocks.en: Reconstruction requires a large amount of historical manufacturing and characterization data, submitted as a supplement in CTD Module 3.2.S.2.6 / 3.2.P.2.

blocks.zh: 不同法規機構對 ECs 的認定可能不同，造成跨地區維護的複雜度。
blocks.en: Different regulators may identify ECs differently, which makes maintenance across regions more complex.

blocks.zh: 比喻：舊房子申請新建築規範
blocks.en: Analogy: An Old House Applying for the New Building Code

blocks.zh: 新建案可以一開始就符合最新建築法規；但一棟 1980 年代的老建築若想享有新規範的某些彈性（如免申報小幅改建），必須先補做結構安全評估、更新竣工圖——這就是 Legacy Product 導入 EC 的過程。工程浩大，但一旦完成，未來的改裝就輕鬆多了。
blocks.en: A new building can comply with the latest building regulations from day one. But a building from the 1980s that wants some of the flexibility under the new rules (such as no filing for minor renovations) must first complete a structural safety assessment and update its as-built drawings. That is what introducing ECs for a legacy product involves. It is a big job, but once it is done, future modifications become much easier.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：什麼時候值得補做 EC？
blocks.en: Key Point: When Is It Worth Adding ECs?

blocks.zh: TR91 明確指出：單獨為了加 EC 而提交先前核准申請，通常效益不高。最佳時機是「搭便車」——當你已經要提交一個重大變更（Major Change）的 PAC 時，順便在同一份申請中加入 EC 清單。這樣既能利用現有審查程序，又能立即享受 EC 帶來的未來申報簡化。
blocks.en: TR91 states clearly that submitting a previously approved application solely to add ECs is usually not worth the effort. The best opportunity is to "piggyback": when you are already submitting a PAC for a Major Change, add the EC list to the same application. This makes use of the existing review procedure and lets you benefit immediately from the simplified future filings that ECs bring.

blocks.zh: Parameter-based EC（參數型）：直接在 filing 中列出具體製程參數值（如攪拌速度 X rpm）——改了就要申報。
blocks.en: Parameter-based EC: specific process parameter values are listed directly in the filing (e.g., mixing speed X rpm), so any change must be filed.

blocks.zh: Performance-based EC（效能型）：改以產品效能或功能性指標為 EC（如「最終產品無菌性符合 USP <71>」）——製程參數調整只要效能達標，可在 PQS 內管理，無需申報。後者是 ICH Q12 的理想狀態。
blocks.en: Performance-based EC: product performance or functionality criteria serve as the EC instead (e.g., "the final product meets sterility requirements per USP <71>"). Process parameters can then be adjusted and managed within the PQS as long as performance is met, with no filing required. The latter is the ideal state under ICH Q12.

blocks.zh: 你的廠區承接一個已上市 8 年的生物製劑客戶產品。客戶希望利用這次製程優化的機會，同步導入 ICH Q12 EC 框架。你如何協助客戶評估哪些 CTD 章節需要補充歷史數據？這項工作應納入哪個合約里程碑？
blocks.en: Your site has taken on a biologic product from a client that has been on the market for 8 years. The client wants to use this process optimization as an opportunity to introduce the ICH Q12 EC framework at the same time. How would you help the client assess which CTD sections need supplementary historical data? Which contract milestone should this work be included in?

blocks.zh: 8.0 Recommendations for Harmonization (Categorization of Changes) 8.0 調和化建議（變更分類）
blocks.en: 8.0 Recommendations for Harmonization (Categorization of Changes)

blocks.zh: 比喻：一個變更，五年才能全球上路
blocks.en: Analogy: One Change, Five Years to Go Global

blocks.zh: 想像你的公司在 2026 年初批准了一項製程改善，理論上可以提升品質並降低成本。在美國 6 個月後獲批、歐盟 8 個月後獲批，但在某個非 ICH 市場，你等了 5 年——這 5 年內，你只能對該市場維持舊製程，或面臨供貨中斷。
blocks.en: Imagine your company approves a process improvement in early 2026 that in theory improves quality and lowers cost. It is approved in the US after 6 months and in the EU after 8 months, but in one non-ICH market you wait 5 years. During those 5 years you can only keep the old process for that market, or face a supply interruption.

blocks.zh: 這就是為什麼 PDA 把「全球法規調和」列為行業最緊迫的倡議之一。
blocks.en: This is why PDA ranks "global regulatory harmonization" among the industry's most urgent initiatives.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：CDMO 的最高複雜度場景
blocks.en: Key Point: The Highest-Complexity Scenario for a CDMO

blocks.zh: 對於 CDMO 來說，挑戰是指數級的：一項對共用設備或廠房的改善，可能同時觸發所有使用該設備的客戶產品的 PAC 義務。10 個客戶、5 個市場 = 潛在 50 份並行申報。這就是為什麼 Site Master File（SMF）策略對 CDMO 如此關鍵——SMF 提供一個共用的廠房基線文件，客戶申報時可引用，減少重複工作。
blocks.en: For a CDMO the challenge is exponential: an improvement to shared equipment or a shared facility can trigger PAC obligations for every client product that uses it. 10 clients × 5 markets = potentially 50 parallel filings. This is why a Site Master File (SMF) strategy is so critical for a CDMO: the SMF provides a shared baseline document for the site that clients can reference in their filings, reducing duplicated work.

blocks.zh: 你的廠區計畫更換一台所有生物製劑產品共用的超濾系統。這個變更會影響 8 個客戶的 12 個產品。你會如何設計「一份科學論據包」讓各客戶可以分別申報？SMF 在這個策略中扮演什麼角色？
blocks.en: Your site plans to replace an ultrafiltration system shared by all biologic products. The change affects 12 products belonging to 8 clients. How would you design a "single scientific package" that lets each client file separately? What role does the SMF play in this strategy?

blocks.zh: 核心概念：全球 PAC 分類的三層架構
blocks.en: Core Concept: The Three-Tier Structure of Global PAC Categorization

blocks.zh: 儘管各地用詞不同，TR91 歸納出一個普遍適用的三層模型：
blocks.en: Although the terminology differs from region to region, TR91 summarizes a generally applicable three-tier model:

blocks.zh: PDA 的建議是：全球法規機構應採用這套共同語言，才能實現真正的調和。
blocks.en: PDA's recommendation is that regulators worldwide adopt this common language in order to achieve true harmonization.

blocks.zh: 8.1 Harmonized Definitions and Consistent Requirements for Approval of Changes 8.1 調和化定義與變更核准一致性要求
blocks.en: 8.1 Harmonized Definitions and Consistent Requirements for Approval of Changes

blocks.zh: 核心概念：定義統一的價值
blocks.en: Core Concept: The Value of Unified Definitions

blocks.zh: 目前最大的問題之一是：「major change」在 FDA 的定義，和 EMA 的 Type II，和某些非 ICH 國家的理解，並不完全對等。這迫使企業為每個地區分別準備科學論據包，大量重複工作。
blocks.en: One of the biggest problems at present is that a "major change" as defined by the FDA, a Type II variation in the EMA, and the understanding in some non-ICH countries are not fully equivalent. This forces companies to prepare a separate scientific package for each region, which involves a great deal of duplicated work.

blocks.zh: PDA 建議的目標：一份科學論據（Single Scientific Package）可以跨地區提交——這對 CDMO 尤其有價值，因為一次做好可以服務所有客戶。
blocks.en: PDA's recommended goal is a Single Scientific Package that can be submitted across regions. This is especially valuable for a CDMO, because doing it right once can serve all clients.

blocks.zh: 穩定性資料標準化的關鍵性
blocks.en: Why Standardizing Stability Data Matters

blocks.zh: 目前最大的差異之一來自穩定性資料要求。ICH 地區接受 3-6 個月實時數據支持重大變更；部分非 ICH 地區要求完整效期數據（可能長達 24-36 個月）。統一的穩定性資料要求能讓企業提前規劃批次安排，大幅縮短「資料缺口等待期」。
blocks.en: One of the biggest differences today comes from stability data requirements. ICH regions accept 3-6 months of real-time data to support a major change, while some non-ICH regions require data covering the full shelf life (possibly as long as 24-36 months). Harmonized stability data requirements would let companies plan batch schedules in advance and greatly shorten the "data gap waiting period".

blocks.zh: 8.2 Mutual Recognition and Consistent Review Times of PACs in ICH Regions 8.2 ICH 區域核准後變更（PAC）之相互認可與一致審查時程
blocks.en: 8.2 Mutual Recognition and Consistent Review Times of PACs in ICH Regions

blocks.zh: 核心概念：相互認可（Mutual Recognition）
blocks.en: Core Concept: Mutual Recognition

blocks.zh: 相互認可的邏輯：如果 FDA 已經審查並批准了一項重大變更，EMA 是否需要從頭再審一遍相同的科學論據？PDA 認為不需要——應建立機制讓 EMA 直接「承認 FDA 的審查結論」。
blocks.en: The logic of mutual recognition: if the FDA has already reviewed and approved a major change, does the EMA need to review the same scientific rationale again from scratch? PDA believes it does not, and that a mechanism should be established so the EMA can directly "recognize the FDA's review conclusions".

blocks.zh: 這個概念其實已有先例：藥品出口證明（Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product，CPP）——許多非 ICH 國家在審查進口藥品時，直接採信發證國（如美國、歐盟）的 GMP 合規證明，不再重複驗廠。PAC 的相互認可是同樣邏輯的延伸。
blocks.en: This concept already has a precedent: the Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product (CPP). When reviewing imported medicines, many non-ICH countries directly accept the GMP compliance certification of the issuing country (e.g., the US or EU) and do not repeat the site inspection. Mutual recognition of PACs is an extension of the same logic.

blocks.zh: 比喻：大學學歷相互認可
blocks.en: Analogy: Mutual Recognition of University Degrees

blocks.zh: 就像部分國家簽訂學歷互認協定——你的台大碩士學歷，不需要在另一個國家重新考試才能認定學術資格。PAC 相互認可是同樣的概念：一個法規機構的嚴格審查，應能作為其他機構的參考依據。
blocks.en: It is like countries that sign degree recognition agreements: your master's degree from National Taiwan University does not need to be re-examined in another country for your academic qualification to be recognized. Mutual recognition of PACs is the same idea: one regulator's rigorous review should serve as a reference for other regulators.

blocks.zh: 重點提示：Table 8.2-1🔍 的實務意義
blocks.en: Key Point: Practical Significance of Table 8.2-1🔍

blocks.zh: 這張表代表 PDA 的理想目標狀態：
blocks.en: This table represents PDA's ideal target state:

blocks.zh: Do and Record：不需審查，PQS 內管理
blocks.en: Do and Record: no review needed, managed within the PQS

blocks.zh: Do and Tell（通知）：最多 90 天
blocks.en: Do and Tell (notification): up to 90 days

blocks.zh: Tell, Wait and Do（事前核准）：最多 180 天
blocks.en: Tell, Wait and Do (prior approval): up to 180 days

blocks.zh: 目前現實與此目標的差距，在部分非 ICH 地區可達 5 年。這個差距就是 PDA 倡議調和的動力所在。
blocks.en: The gap between this target and the current reality can reach 5 years in some non-ICH regions. That gap is what drives PDA's call for harmonization.

blocks.zh: 策略思考
blocks.en: Strategic Reflection

blocks.zh: 假設明年起 ICH 成員間正式建立 PAC 相互認可機制。你的公司應如何調整全球申報策略？你會優先在哪個 ICH 國家首先提交重大變更，以「首先獲批→帶動其他 ICH 成員認可」？這個選擇應考量哪些因素（審查速度、機構能力、產品市場優先順序）？
blocks.en: Suppose a PAC mutual recognition mechanism is formally established among ICH members from next year. How should your company adjust its global filing strategy? In which ICH country would you submit a major change first, so that "first approval drives recognition by the other ICH members"? What factors should this choice consider (review speed, regulator capability, product market priorities)?

blocks.zh: 9.0 Conclusion 9.0 結論
blocks.en: 9.0 Conclusion

blocks.zh: 核心概念：TR91 的最終訊息
blocks.en: Core Concept: The Final Message of TR91

blocks.zh: TR91 的結論把 PAC 管理提升到「持續改善文化」的高度：
blocks.en: The conclusion of TR91 raises PAC management to the level of a "culture of continual improvement":

blocks.zh: PAC 不只是法規合規問題，更是製造卓越與病患可及性的關鍵推手。
blocks.en: PAC is not only a regulatory compliance issue but a key enabler of manufacturing excellence and patient access.

blocks.zh: ICH Q12（含 PACMP）是實現全球一致審查的路線圖。
blocks.en: ICH Q12 (including the PACMP) is the roadmap for achieving globally consistent review.

blocks.zh: 法規調和是目標，CDMO 的職責是在調和完成之前，做好現有多元系統下的管理。
blocks.en: Regulatory harmonization is the goal; until it is achieved, the CDMO's responsibility is to manage well within the existing, diverse systems.

blocks.zh: CDMO Operations Director 的視角
blocks.en: The CDMO Operations Director's Perspective

blocks.zh: TR91 的整個 Section 4 對 CDMO 有一個核心提醒：你的法規能力本身就是差異化競爭力。當客戶面對複雜的全球 PAC 管理時，能夠提供「CDMO 主導的 PAC 策略規劃——從 EC 設計到多地區申報包——並有效管理 SMF 與品質協議」的夥伴，遠比只能執行製造的 CDMO 更有價值。
blocks.en: The whole of Section 4 of TR91 carries one core reminder for a CDMO: your regulatory capability is itself a differentiating competitive strength. When clients face complex global PAC management, a partner that can offer "CDMO-led PAC strategy planning, from EC design to multi-region filing packages, while effectively managing the SMF and quality agreements" is far more valuable than a CDMO that can only execute manufacturing.

blocks.zh: 10.0 References 10.0 參考文獻
blocks.en: 10.0 References

blocks.zh: 核心參考文獻導覽
blocks.en: Guide to the Key References

blocks.zh: TR91 的 32 條參考文獻構成了一個完整的全球 PAC 知識體系：
blocks.en: The 32 references in TR91 form a complete body of knowledge on global PAC management:

blocks.zh: Ref. 4 & 5（WHO）：生物製劑與疫苗的 PAC 指引——非 ICH 地區最重要的橋接文件。
blocks.en: Ref. 4 & 5 (WHO): PAC guidelines for biotherapeutic products and vaccines, the most important bridging documents for non-ICH regions.

blocks.zh: Ref. 6（ICH Q12）：全書核心框架，EC 與 PACMP 的定義來源。
blocks.en: Ref. 6 (ICH Q12): the core framework of the whole report and the source of the EC and PACMP definitions.

blocks.zh: Ref. 11（FDA EC 草稿指引）：Established Conditions 的美國版詮釋。
blocks.en: Ref. 11 (FDA draft EC guidance): the US interpretation of Established Conditions.

blocks.zh: Ref. 13（EMA PACMP Q&A）：歐盟 PACMP 實施細節。
blocks.en: Ref. 13 (EMA PACMP Q&A): implementation details of the PACMP in the EU.

blocks.zh: Ref. 20（Health Canada NOC）：加拿大的 PAC 分類文件，與 WHO 格式相似。
blocks.en: Ref. 20 (Health Canada NOC): Canada's PAC categorization document, similar in format to the WHO guidance.

blocks.zh: Ref. 26（PDA 2021 Survey）：行業調查數據來源，支持「部分地區審查超過 5 年」的論述。
blocks.en: Ref. 26 (PDA 2021 Survey): the source of industry survey data supporting the statement that "review takes more than 5 years in some regions".

blocks.zh: Ref. 27–31（SUPAC & EU Variation Regulation）：藥學 PAC 科學資料的具體要求文件。
blocks.en: Ref. 27-31 (SUPAC & EU Variation Regulation): documents setting out the specific requirements for pharmaceutical PAC scientific data.

blocks.zh: CDMO 建議閱讀優先順序
blocks.en: Recommended Reading Order for a CDMO

blocks.zh:
如果你只能精讀三份原始文件，建議優先選擇：
ICH Q12（Ref. 6）→ FDA EC 指引（Ref. 11）→ EMA PACMP Q&A（Ref. 13）。
這三份文件覆蓋了 ICH 成員區域 80% 以上的主要產品市場，也是理解 EC 設計與 PACMP 策略的基礎。
blocks.en:
If you can only read three source documents in depth, start with:
ICH Q12 (Ref. 6) → FDA EC guidance (Ref. 11) → EMA PACMP Q&A (Ref. 13).
These three documents cover the major product markets of more than 80% of ICH member regions and are the foundation for understanding EC design and PACMP strategy.

blocks.zh: Section 4 總結 — Global PAC Management, Harmonization & Conclusion
blocks.en: Section 4 Summary: Global PAC Management, Harmonization & Conclusion

blocks.zh: ICH 成員區域的優勢：以風險為基礎的申報分類、有限穩定性資料接受度、明確審查時程——是高效 PAC 管理的基礎條件。CDMO 必須精通這套系統，並能同時管理美國（FDA）、歐盟（EMA）、加拿大（Health Canada）、日本（PMDA）的並行申報。
blocks.en: Strengths of the ICH member regions: risk-based filing categorization, acceptance of limited stability data, and clear review timelines are the basic conditions for efficient PAC management. A CDMO must master this system and be able to manage parallel filings in the US (FDA), EU (EMA), Canada (Health Canada) and Japan (PMDA) at the same time.

blocks.zh: 非 ICH 地區的現實：缺乏指引、審查可能長達 5 年、逐件序列審查的要求，使全球同步申報極為困難。供應鏈影響是最直接的患者風險，應提早與非 ICH 機構溝通。WHO 指引可作為橋接工具。
blocks.en: The reality in non-ICH regions: the lack of guidance, reviews that can take up to 5 years, and the requirement for sequential, one-by-one review make simultaneous global filing extremely difficult. Supply chain impact is the most direct patient risk, so communicate with non-ICH regulators early. WHO guidance can serve as a bridging tool.

blocks.zh: Legacy Products 的 EC 導入策略：最佳時機是「搭便車」——與重大 PAC 同步提交 EC 清單。歷史製造數據是論據基礎，Parameter-based EC 可升級為 Performance-based EC 以獲得更大靈活性。
blocks.en: EC introduction strategy for legacy products: the best opportunity is to "piggyback" by submitting the EC list together with a major PAC. Historical manufacturing data is the basis of the rationale, and Parameter-based ECs can be upgraded to Performance-based ECs for greater flexibility.

blocks.zh: PDA 調和建議：統一 major/moderate/minor 的全球定義，以及相互認可機制——一個 ICH 成員的批准，應能簡化其他成員的審查。目標審查時程：通知類 ≤90 天，事前核准類 ≤180 天。
blocks.en: PDA harmonization recommendations: harmonized global definitions of major/moderate/minor changes, and a mutual recognition mechanism, so that approval by one ICH member should simplify review by the others. Target review timelines: up to 90 days for notification-type changes and up to 180 days for prior-approval-type changes.

blocks.zh: CDMO 的核心競爭力：共用設備/廠房變更可能同時觸發所有相關產品的 PAC 義務，Site Master File（SMF）策略是管理多客戶複雜度的關鍵工具。法規能力本身是 CDMO 差異化的核心資產。
blocks.en: The CDMO's core competitiveness: changes to shared equipment or facilities can trigger PAC obligations for all related products at once, and a Site Master File (SMF) strategy is the key tool for managing multi-client complexity. Regulatory capability is itself a core differentiating asset for a CDMO.
